chunks: Go to the shadow with three ramifications
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the shadow with three branches in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration, often cited in Shia hadith collections such as those of Al-Kulayni, interprets the 'shadow with three branches' as a metaphor for the intercession and protection of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically the Prophet Muhammad, Imam Ali, and the two Imams Hasan and Husayn. It highlights the theological concept that on the Day of Judgment, when the sun draws near, believers will find refuge under the spiritual authority of the Imams, mirroring the shade of the Tree of Tuba. This interpretation underscores the unique status of the Imams as the primary sources of divine guidance and salvation for the faithful.
